text.p: The Athens stock exchange is considering the launch of a "probationary board" where shares of listed companies which have violated bourse regulations will trade, it said on Thursday.

The rationale for setting up such a board is to inform the investing public that investment in such companies entails higher risks as they appear unable or unwilling to comply with Athens stock exchange rules, it said.
"This way, for a certain time period, we will avoid trading suspensions in these shares in an effort to curtail the emergence of an off-exchange black market for the shares," the bourse said.
However, if the companies fail to meet regulations by a deadline set by the exchange board, the bourse will then reconsider a trading suspension or other measures including delisting.
